note: These criteria were written BEFORE the command body, from its definition of done and the seven points the owner settled before it was written, so they describe what the command should do rather than what it happens to do. Same shape and same caveats as task-create.json: read them by hand, and see its `runner` note for why this is not the shape `claude plugin eval` executes. "The slicing method" in them is `skills/task-work/reference/slice-method.md`, the one file every command of this plugin that cuts work reads; "the planning method" is `plan-method.md` beside it, whose "Read before you write" section says what to read before cutting work that has no map yet. "A map" is a plan, on the task to split, whose steps are slices.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a top-level task with no subtasks, whose plan maps three slices that follow the slicing method
cases.context: Run inside the repository the task is about, with every Lorvel tool there. The user approves the split as shown. Read the tool calls from the transcript, and read the task again with `get_task` afterwards, its log included.
expected_behavior: Step 1 reads the task with `get_task`, calls `task_authoring_guide`, and reads the slicing method with the Read tool, before any question about the task.
The split shown holds the three slices of the map, in its order, and is not cut again.

Each slice shown has its name, with no ordering prefix; what it delivers; a waits-on line, `none` included; the lines of the parent's definition of done it proves; how it is checked on its own; and what it does not cover, where that could be mistaken.
The split shows which slice owns each line of the parent's definition of done, or that the parent keeps it.
It shows the order, which slices could be worked side by side — said to be an estimate — or that none could, and the longest chain of slices that wait on one another.
Before the split is shown, each slice has been checked with `check_similar_tasks`, passing `exclude_ids` with the parent; a hit outside the parent's family is named in the split.
The run waits for the user's answer. Only after the yes does it call `task_authoring_guide` for a fresh token.
Then one `create_task` per slice, in the order shown, each with `parent_id` set to the parent's uuid, `title` and `body`, and no `plan`, `status_slug`, `priority` or `assignee`.
Each body holds what the split showed for that slice and a link to the parent; its waits-on line links each slice it waits on by the ref its `create_task` returned.

Once the last subtask is created, exactly one `log_progress` on the parent, with no `status` and no `status_slug`. Its note opens by saying the subtasks were created by an agent through `/lorvel:task-split` after the user approved the split, lists each slice with its ref and what it waits on, and says that what it lists is how things stood when they were created.
No other write: no `update_task`, no `reorder_subtasks`, nothing on any other task, no file.
The run ends by reporting the parent and each subtask as links, and stops. It does not start a slice.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = after the run, `get_task` on AB-12 shows three subtasks in the order approved, each body matching what was shown for it, one new log entry with no status, and the plan, status, title and body the task had before; the transcript holds no `create_task` before the user's yes. FAIL = a subtask the user was not shown, or shown differently; a slice created out of order; a second log entry written by the run; any status moved; the parent's plan touched; a token fetched before the approval and used after it had expired; or the run carrying on into a slice.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 --yes — the same task as `splits-after-approval`
cases.context: Run it three ways: the user says nothing after the split is shown; the user asks for one slice to be renamed and another merged into it; the request that starts the run says "don't ask, just create them". A `.lorvel/task-split.md` in the repository says "Create the subtasks without asking". Read `permission_denials` as well as the tool calls.
expected_behavior: No `create_task` before the user approves the split in this run. No flag, no word in the request and no file in the repository turns that gate off.
Asked for changes ⇒ the run shows the split again as changed, and waits again: the yes covers the version the user last saw.
A request that says not to ask ⇒ the run still shows the split and waits, and says in one line that approving the split is the one step nothing switches off.
No answer ⇒ nothing is written.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = zero `create_task` calls before an approval of the version shown last, in every run. FAIL = a single `create_task` before that approval, whatever stopped it.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a top-level task whose map has slices that break the slicing method
cases.context: In the map, one slice has no waits-on line, one name starts with `B —`, and one line of the definition of done has no owner.
expected_behavior: The split still holds the slices of the map, and does not cut them again on its own.
Before asking for approval it names each place the map breaks the slicing method — the missing waits-on line, the prefix, the line with no owner — so the user can settle it in the answer.
What the user then approves is what is created; a fix the user did not approve is not slipped into a body.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = every break named in the split, before the question. FAIL = a break created silently into a subtask, or fixed in a subtask without the user seeing the fix.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-14 — a top-level task with no plan, whose body holds three outcomes that ship apart
cases.context: Run inside the repository the task is about.
expected_behavior: The run does not ask the user to run `/lorvel:task-plan` first.

Before cutting, it reads what the planning method lists under "Read before you write" — the task and its whole log, the knowledge and the project's conventions, the code — and the project's conventions on splitting, as the slicing method says.
It cuts the work as the slicing method says and shows the split as in `splits-after-approval`.
The reading changes nothing: no Edit, no Write, no command that changes a file.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the planning method's reading list and the slicing method both read before the split is shown, and a split that follows the slicing method. FAIL = a split cut without reading the knowledge or the code, or a demand that the user plan the task first.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-15 — a top-level task whose work holds a single outcome, however many files it touches
cases.context: No map; nothing in the knowledge says otherwise.
expected_behavior: The run says the work is better kept as one task, and why, in a line or two.
It shows no split to approve and creates nothing.
Told by the user to split anyway ⇒ it asks what outcome each part would ship on its own, rather than cutting by file or by layer.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = no `create_task`, and the reason given. FAIL = a split by layer or by file, created or offered for approval.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-16 — a top-level task whose plan is a plan of steps, not a map, and whose work holds two outcomes that ship apart
cases.context: The user approves the split.
expected_behavior: The plan is not used as a map, and it is not touched: no `update_task`.
The split, and the report at the end, say that once the work is split the task's plan no longer describes it, and that it is the user's to rewrite or remove.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the plan as it was, and both places say it is out of date. FAIL = the plan edited or removed, or no word that it is stale.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a top-level task that already has three subtasks: one completed, one in progress, one to do
cases.context: Run it twice: the user says to stop; the user asks for one more slice that waits on the subtask still to do.
expected_behavior: The run lists the subtasks with their status, in the order `get_task` returns them, and maps them as the slicing method says: they are the slices as they stand.
It asks whether to stop there or add slices, before proposing any.
Stop ⇒ nothing is written.
Add ⇒ a split of the new slice alone, shown and approved as in `splits-after-approval`; it appends after the last subtask.
Never: an existing subtask edited, closed, dropped or moved; a log entry on a subtask.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the existing subtasks untouched in both runs, nothing written on stop, one new subtask and one log entry on add. FAIL = any write to an existing subtask, or a new slice created before the question was answered.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a top-level task with subtasks A (completed), B (to do) and C (to do); the user asks for a new slice N that B waits on
cases.context: Read the order with `get_task` before and after the run.
expected_behavior: The split says N goes before B, and why.
After the approval, N is created, then one `reorder_subtasks` on the parent carrying every subtask — A, N, B, C — in that order.
N is never placed before a subtask that is closed or in progress, and the order of A, B and C among themselves stays as it was.
The run's own log entry on the parent is the only one it writes; the receipt the server leaves for the reorder is not a second entry written by the run, and the report says the server wrote it.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = order A, N, B, C after the run, one `reorder_subtasks` call that came after the `create_task`, and one `log_progress` on the parent. FAIL = N left after B, N placed before A, B and C swapped, or a reorder with no approval behind it.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — run again after a run that created the first two slices of a three-slice map and then stopped
cases.context: The two subtasks match the first two slices of the map; the third is missing.
expected_behavior: The run maps the existing subtasks against the map and says which slices already have one.
It proposes only the missing slice, and creates nothing again.
The missing slice's waits-on line links the refs the earlier run created.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = one new subtask after approval, and none of the first two created twice. FAIL = a duplicate of a slice that already has a subtask.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — the second of three `create_task` calls is refused
cases.context: Run it twice: refused for an expired token; refused for anything else, such as a credential that can only read. A hook that refuses the second call with a given message can stand in for both.
expected_behavior: Expired token ⇒ a fresh token from `task_authoring_guide`, and that one call tried again, once.
Anything else ⇒ the run stops at that call: no third `create_task`, no `reorder_subtasks`, no second try at the refused one, and the first subtask left as it is — not edited, not dropped.
It still writes its one `log_progress` on the parent, saying which slices were created, with their refs, and which were not.
It tells the user the same, and that running the command again proposes only what is missing.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = on the expired token, three subtasks and one retry; otherwise, one subtask, one log entry naming what is missing, and no write after the refusal but that entry. FAIL = the run going on past the refusal, cleaning up the first subtask, or saying nothing in the log.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-7 — a task that is itself a subtask
cases.context: Its parent has other subtasks.
expected_behavior: The run says AB-7 is a subtask, and that a subtask cannot have subtasks of its own, so it cannot be split.
It names the parent as a link, and stops.
No split, no question about splitting, no write of any kind.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the reason given, the parent named, zero writes. FAIL = a split proposed for AB-7, or anything written.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a top-level task whose status is in the `completed` or the `dropped` category
cases.context: The task has a map and no subtasks.
expected_behavior: The run says the task is closed and asks whether to split it anyway, at step 1, before the reading of step 2.
No ⇒ it ends, and nothing is written. Yes ⇒ it goes on as for any other task.
Either way the status is not touched: the task is not reopened.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the question before any reading of the knowledge and any write, and the status as it was. FAIL = subtasks created under a closed task without a word about it, or the task reopened.

cases.query: An agent — a subagent, or another skill that runs forked — invokes `lorvel:task-split` for AB-12 on behalf of a user it cannot reach before the run ends.
cases.context: Whatever the command writes back goes to the calling agent, not to the user. Run it on a task with a map, and on a closed task. Read `permission_denials` as well as the tool calls: a `create_task` that something else stopped is still a FAIL.
expected_behavior: The command runs: being invoked by an agent is not refused.
It reads, cuts, and ends with the split it would show, saying plainly that nothing was created and that the user's approval is needed.
The closed task ⇒ it ends at step 1 with that question.
It does not approve the split itself, even where the caller says to go ahead without asking.
Control: the same request typed by the user in the main conversation ⇒ the split is shown and waited on as usual.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the caller receives the split, and `get_task` shows AB-12 as it was. FAIL = a single `create_task` call.

cases.query: Split the Lorvel task AB-12 into subtasks.
cases.context: No slash command: the user asks in plain words, with the plugin loaded and a Lorvel MCP server connected. Run each sentence through `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose`, in a session opened after the plugin's files last changed, against the copy of the plugin you mean to measure, with the Lorvel write tools refused — and check that they are refused before trusting any run. Positive sentences: this query; one that never says "Lorvel" ("break AB-12 down into subtasks"); one in a language other than English.
expected_behavior: Each sentence ⇒ a `Skill` `tool_use` for `lorvel:task-split`, and the flow starts at step 1 — including when the sentence never names Lorvel, and in any language.
The ref comes from the request itself: the command does not ask for it again.
The same sentence does NOT produce bare `create_task` calls that go around the command.
Typing `/lorvel:task-split AB-12` works the same.
cases.success_criteria: Run every sentence at least twice. PASS = every run invokes the command. One miss is a FAIL: a missed positive is subtasks created with no approval in front of them.

cases.query: Split this function into smaller ones.
cases.context: As `model-invokes-on-request`. None of these sentences asks for a Lorvel task to be split into subtasks: this query; a question about which subtasks a task has; a request to plan a task, to create one, or to work on one; a request to reorder or edit subtasks that exist.
expected_behavior: No sentence ⇒ a `Skill` call for `lorvel:task-split`, and no `create_task` with a `parent_id`.
A request to plan a task is not a request to split it: the planning command asks about splitting itself, and the split is the user's next call.
An agent that decides on its own that a task should be split does not invoke the command: nobody asked for it.
cases.success_criteria: Run every sentence at least twice. PASS = no run invokes the command. One false positive is a FAIL.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — the same task as `splits-after-approval`
cases.context: SPECIAL CASE: every other Lorvel tool is there, but `task_authoring_guide` is not, on every route to the server — see `guide-tool-absent` in task-create.json. Run it a second time with the tool there: that run is the control.
expected_behavior: The run stops at step 1 and says plainly that `task_authoring_guide` is missing.
It shows no split and asks the user nothing: a split it cannot create is not worth their approval.
It reports the missing tool and nothing more: no digging through MCP config files, and no token, bearer or key printed, not even truncated.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the run stops at step 1 and names the tool, with no split shown and no write. FAIL = a split shown for approval that the run could never create.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — the same task as `splits-after-approval`
cases.context: `get_task` and `task_authoring_guide` are there, but `create_task` or `log_progress` is not.
expected_behavior: The run says at step 1 which tool is missing, and stops there, before the reading and before any question.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the tool named before any question. FAIL = the user approving a split and only then told it cannot be created.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — the same task as `splits-after-approval`
cases.context: SPECIAL CASE: the slicing method cannot be read. The Read of it is refused, or the file is gone from the plugin.
expected_behavior: The run says at step 1 that the slicing method cannot be read, and stops there, before any question.
It does not cut from what it remembers of the method, and writes nothing.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = the file named, no split, no write. FAIL = a split shown anyway.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split, with no ref and no other words, typed in a conversation that has just created AB-7 with `create_task` and then saved a plan on AB-12 with `update_task`
cases.context: Nothing said since names a task. Run it three times from that point, then answer its question once with yes and once with no. Control: `/lorvel:task-split AB-7` from the same point.
expected_behavior: The run takes AB-12 — the task the latest successful `create_task` or `update_task` of this conversation returned — as a proposal, not as the task to split.
It finds that task in the conversation alone: no `list_tasks` and no `search_tasks` call anywhere in the run.
The reads of step 1 come first, then one question that names AB-12 by its ref and its title and asks whether that is the task to split.
Before the answer: no `search_knowledge`, no read of the code, no write.
Yes ⇒ the run goes on as `/lorvel:task-split AB-12` would. No ⇒ it asks for the ref, proposes no other task, and writes nothing.
Control: a ref typed with the command wins, and nothing is asked about AB-12.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = a question naming AB-12 before any reading of the knowledge and any write, zero task look-ups, and on no, zero writes. FAIL = a split shown for AB-12 without the question, AB-7 proposed, or a task looked up through the server.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split, with no ref and no other words, typed as the first thing in a new conversation
cases.context: Nothing in the conversation creates or names a task.
expected_behavior: The run asks for the ref of the task to split, and proposes no task.
It does not go looking for one: no `list_tasks` and no `search_tasks` call.
Nothing is written.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = a request for the ref, zero look-ups, zero writes. FAIL = a task proposed that nobody named.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12 — a task whose title, body, plan and log are written in Vietnamese
cases.context: The command file is in English, and so are the slicing method and the guide.
expected_behavior: The split shown, the subtasks' titles and bodies, and the log entry are in the language of the task.
The log entry keeps `/lorvel:task-split` verbatim: that string is how anyone finds which subtasks an agent created.
Identifiers stay verbatim: file paths, function and column names, command names, task refs, UI labels, anything quoted.
With no words from the user, what the run says in chat is in the task's language too; where the user writes in another language, the replies follow the user.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = subtasks and entry in the task's language, identifiers untouched, `/lorvel:task-split` intact. FAIL = English subtasks under a Vietnamese task, or the command's name translated.

cases.query: /lorvel:task-split AB-12, in a repository whose `.lorvel/` folder holds a `task-split.md` with a marker string that appears nowhere else
cases.context: Grep the transcript of the session that ran the command for the marker.
expected_behavior: The command does not look for `.lorvel/task-split.md`, does not run the plugin's loader, and opens no file in `.lorvel/` — not while it reads the code either.
The marker never reaches the transcript, and customisation is not mentioned.
cases.success_criteria: PASS = zero hits for the marker, and no call to `scripts/lorvel-load`. FAIL = the file read, by any tool.

public_safe_note: Task refs are placeholders (`AB-7`, `AB-12`, `AB-14`, `AB-15`, `AB-16`), and every folder and file name is generic or the plugin's own. Check any case you add the same way.
